transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Hernandez, thank you for coming in. I also want to thank your daughter for helping us communicate today. I have asked my senior colleague to be here with us.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Gracias.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I need to talk with you about the contrast dye we gave you for your scan earlier today. We made a medical error. We gave you the contrast agent even though your blood tests showed that your kidneys were not functioning well enough to handle it safely.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: ¿Qué? ¿Qué pasó?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She is asking what happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am saying that we gave her a medication that could put her kidneys at risk because we did not follow the safety protocol for patients with high creatinine levels. Creatinine is a waste product in the blood; when it is high, it means the kidneys are struggling, and the dye can make that worse. Does that make sense so far, or should I explain that part differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. I thought the scan was okay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She says she thought everything was fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is very difficult to hear this, and I know this is unexpected. To make sure we are on the same page, do you understand that the dye we used might have caused a problem with how your kidneys are working?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. Is she okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring her. I am sorry for any confusion this has caused. We were very busy in the radiology suite today, and the check for her kidney function was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Busy? My mother is sick. Why would you just forget to check?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why was this missed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that feels unfair. It is frustrating to hear that the team was busy when your mother's safety should have come first.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am scared. I don't want her kidneys to fail.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely normal to feel scared right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what do we do now? How do we fix it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep a close eye on her.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? Do you have a plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are just going to see how the numbers look on the next test.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When is the next test? Tomorrow? Today?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will likely do another blood draw soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Soon is not a time. I need to know if she needs more medicine or more water.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will let you know when the doctor reviews the labs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not helpful. You made a mistake and now you are telling us to just wait.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is an incredibly stressful moment for both of you. I can see how worried you are about your mother's health.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know exactly what is happening to her kidneys right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have to wait for the chemistry panel to come back from the lab.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see. We will stay tuned for the results.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient/daughter to finish their turns and remains regulated under pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, used lay language (waste product), checked comprehension twice, and avoided false reassurance.

A.justification: A direct apology was offered, but it was immediately diluted by an excuse regarding the radiology suite being 'very busy'.

R.justification: Resident specifically named 'frustrating', 'scared', and 'stressful' while referencing the patient's concerns about safety and health.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders such as 'we will see' and 'stay tuned' without specific timelines or a concrete plan.
